title: Create Nodics APIs
readerIntent: Create a governed API without bypassing Nodics routing, authentication, authorization, or ownership layers.
priorKnowledge: Understand schemas, services, facades, controllers, routing, and identity.
owner: Owning business module using Nodics API and router contracts
summary: Define APIs in the owning module, keep transport mapping thin, delegate orchestration and business behavior, and let Nodics enforce exposure, identity, authorization, tenancy, validation, and responses.

sections.heading: Before writing code
items: Confirm the capability owner and search existing schemas, CRUD routes, services, facades, and APIs before adding another path.

Describe method, stable versioned path, request and response contracts, tenant/enterprise scope, principal types, permissions, exposure, limits, errors, idempotency, caching, observability, and compatibility.
Keep human username/password login separate from employee access tokens, module/service credentials, and scheduled-job identity.

sections.heading: Implementation
items: Place route metadata in the owning module and declare controller, action, security, permission, exposure, and API metadata explicitly.
Use a controller only to translate the Nodics request into a facade call; never place domain rules or persistence in it.
Use a facade for orchestration across services and a service for owned business behavior.
Access data only through schema models and database services; do not import a database client.
Use Nodics status/error contracts and expose only approved response fields.
Generate derived controllers, routes, tests, or OpenAPI from authoritative schemas and router definitions; do not hand-edit generated output.

sections.heading: Verification
items: Test success, invalid body/query/header, missing identity, wrong principal type, missing permission, wrong tenant/enterprise, boundary values, contract compatibility, integration, rate/size limits, error masking, and regression.
Verify unauthorized requests fail before controller or business execution.
Regenerate API documentation and update canonical capability documentation whenever the public behavior changes.
